verdict.rationale: BigQuery documents custom quotas that cap the data processed per day at project or user level, which stops runaway on-demand queries from running up costs. A community comment confirms per-query byte limits exist, but notes a looping script can still get around a per-query cap. The $14k-bill anecdote shows the risk when no limits are set; it does not contradict the quota feature. Missing for 10: documented controls for idle or reserved slot compute (auto-suspend or reservation caps), budget alerts or notifications, and independent hands-on proof that quotas actually halted a runaway job.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, budgets, resource monitors, or auto-suspend stop a runaway query or idle compute from burning money overnight

citations.quote: you can manage costs by requesting a custom quota that specifies a limit on the amount of data processed per day
Creating a custom quota on processed data lets you control costs at the project level or at the user level.
you can set a byte-size limit for individual queries plus custom quotas
